    Session handoff: pamlj — pamlmixed() development

    Paste this whole file as your first message in a fresh Claude Code session (in any working directory) to pick up exactly where the previous session left off.

    Where this project lives

    • Repo: /home/mcfanda/Skinner/Forge/jamovi/pamlj/pamlj
    • Branch: Version.1.1.1
    • Package: pamlj, an R + jamovi power-analysis suite (correlation, GLM, mediation, proportions, SEM, mixed models, …). All work described here is in the mixed-model module, pamlmixed() — its R-side implementation is R/S3_mixed.R + R/pamlmixed.f.R, its jamovi-side option/UI definitions are jamovi/pamlmixed.a.yaml, .u.yaml, and jamovi/js/pamlmixed.js.

    Standing workflow rules (established this session, keep following them)

    • Propose, then implement. For non-trivial features, lay out the approach (or use plan mode) and get explicit confirmation before writing code — this repeatedly mattered for naming decisions (e.g. focus vs test) and design tradeoffs (e.g. auto-inflating a replication count vs. erroring clearly).
    • Never commit or push unless explicitly asked. Everything from this session is sitting uncommitted in the working tree — that’s intentional, not an oversight.
    • After any .a.yaml/.u.yaml/jamovi/js/*.js change, regenerate via Rscript -e 'jmvtools::prepare(".")' before testing.
    • Verify by actually running things — devtools::load_all(".") + testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat") (or a targeted Rscript -e reproduction) before claiming anything works. This session caught several real bugs this way (a mis-parsed negative-sign syntax edge case, a multi-GiB future/parallel memory blowup, a crossed-cluster row-count explosion) that would have shipped silently otherwise.
    • One testthat run per change is fine without asking first; don’t loop retries blindly if something fails — diagnose root cause.
    • paper/ is deliberately gitignored (the user added paper/*/paper* to .gitignore mid-session) — don’t “fix” that.

    Declined work — do not implement unless asked again

    Early in this session the user asked about defaulting the mediation module’s path-diagram option (diagram) to FALSE for the R wrapper. After I found the option already existed (jamovi default TRUE, R wrapper default TRUE) and proposed flipping only the R default, the user said “ok do not do anything.” This was explicitly declined — leave it alone.

    What was built this session, in order

    1. pamlmixed(model = <fitted lme4::lmer()/glmer()>) — extracts fixed effects, random-effect variances, residual variance, cluster sizes, and categorical contrast coding directly from a fitted model; defaults aim = "power". Core logic: .mixed_from_fit() in R/S3_mixed.R (near the end of the file — this is the single most important function to read to re-orient).
    2. Custom contrast-coding schemes for categorical predictors: deviation (default), simple, dummy, difference, helmert, repeated, polynomial, or a verbatim custom matrix — selectable via jamovi’s var_type coding column or R’s categorical = list(var = list(levels=, coding=, contrasts=)). .mixed_contrast_matrix() / .mixed_named_contrasts() in R/S3_mixed.R.
    3. jamovi UI: added a Coding column to the var_type ListBox (jamovi/pamlmixed.a.yaml + .u.yaml), narrowed the Levels column, and — via jamovi/js/pamlmixed.js — auto-reset coding to a safe default when not applicable and hid the R-only custom scheme from ever sticking via the GUI (jamovi has no true per-cell enable/disable, confirmed by reading jamovi’s own client source).
    4. Correlated random effects: cor(a,b)=.3 / cov(a,b)=.3 syntax commands correlate two symbol-labeled scalar random terms of the same cluster (extract_syntax_commands() + pamlmixed_makemodel() in R/S3_mixed.R); .mixed_from_fit() now extracts real VarCorr() covariances and emits them as cov() commands automatically.
    5. Fixed a future/parallel Monte Carlo memory bug: .slow_onerun()’s model formula picked up a self-referential/circular environment (fixed via env = baseenv() in pamlmixed_makemodel()), and the parallel closure referenced the entire obj Runner instance unnecessarily (fixed by hoisting test <- obj$info$test out first). This had been causing multi-GiB “exceeds maxSizeOfObjects” warnings for real user models with algo="mc".
    6. focus = "TermName" — the model=-path equivalent of the syntax DSL’s test: command; selects which fixed effect drives an aim="n" sample-size search.
    7. Fixed a crossed-random-effects row-count explosion in .mixed_from_fit(): every clustering factor previously got its own n = nobs/k, and .make_data() multiplied all of them together, squaring the simulated dataset size for genuinely crossed designs (e.g. subject × item). Now only one clustering factor carries the shared replication factor.
    8. Automatic between:/within: cluster detection: .mixed_from_fit() now checks whether a predictor is constant within a clustering factor and auto-marks it between: var|cluster, avoiding spurious “N per cluster too small” failures for item-level or subject-level properties in crossed designs (this exact mechanism was demonstrated interactively by the user before I automated it).
    9. vignettes/mixed_from_lmer.Rmd — a runnable tutorial vignette covering the whole model= workflow, verified to render end-to-end via rmarkdown::render().
    10. paper/pamlmixed_brm_outline.md (approved outline) and paper/pamlmixed_brm_manuscript.Rmd (full prose draft) — a Behavior Research Methods methods paper on pamlmixed(). Headline claim: pamlmixed() automates the search for required sample size (aim="n", a hybrid analytic + Monte Carlo search via int_seek()), which neither simr (manual grid + visual inspection via powerCurve()) nor PANGEA (analytic, no fitted-model extraction) offer in combination; longpower solves for N directly too but only for its closed-form growth-curve design family. Positioning was fact-checked via web search (Green & MacLeod 2016 for simr; Westfall, Kenny & Judd 2014 for PANGEA; Iddi & Donohue 2022 for longpower; Kumle, Võ & Draschkow 2021, published in BRM itself, as closely related prior work). Section 5 (Validation/Simulation Study) is rationale-only prose — no simulations have been run, no numeric results exist yet.

    How to re-orient fast

    1. cd /home/mcfanda/Skinner/Forge/jamovi/pamlj/pamlj && git status && git diff --stat
    2. Read .mixed_from_fit() in R/S3_mixed.R — the load-bearing function for everything in items 1, 4, 6, 7, 8 above.
    3. Read paper/pamlmixed_brm_manuscript.Rmd for the fullest, most polished narrative of what was built, why, and how it’s positioned relative to other tools.
    4. Run devtools::load_all(".") then testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat") to confirm the working tree is still green before making further changes.
